<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- head-51: body_md -->
Let $X' = X \times_K K'$, and let $X'_k = Mlt_k(X')$,
satisfying the conclusion of Proposition \ref{si-dim3.2}.  Let
$j: X' \to X$ be the natural map of difference schemes.  Then
the radicial map 
$j$ induces a bijection between the points of $X'$ and of $X$,
or between the perfectly reduced subschemes of $X'$ and of $X$,
preserving reduced total  dimension.
Let
$Mlt_k X  $ be the perfectly reduced subscheme of $X$ 
corresponding to $Mlt_k X'$.  Then (1),(2),(3) are clear. 
(cf.   \ref{inv-base-change}).   \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-51 -->
<!-- lem-36: body_md -->
\label{trans-mult-n} Let $X={\rm Spec^\sigma \, } R$ be a well-mixed
difference scheme, and assume $X \to B_{n'}(X)$ has total dimension
$\leq n < n'$.  Then for any difference field $L$ and any $L$-valued
point $y_{n'}$ of $B_{n'}(X)$, and $y \in X(L)$ lifting $y_{n'}$,
$\sigma^n( {\cal O}_{X,y} \times_{B_{n'}(X),y_{n'}} L)$ has total
dimension $0$.
<!-- end lem-36 -->
<!-- head-52: body_md -->
By \ref{inv-base-change},
we may take $L$ to be inversive. 

We may assume $X = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } R$, $R$ a well-mixed difference ring.  Let
$R_n = \sigma^n(R)$.  Let $y$ be the unique extension of $y_{n'}$ to a
difference ring morphism $y: R \to L$; let $y_m = y | R_m$.  Let
${\otimes}'$ denote the tensor product in the well-mixed category; $A
{\otimes} '_B C$ is the quotient of $A {\otimes} _B C$ by the smallest
well-mixed ideal of that ring.  Let $S = R {\otimes} ' _{R_{n'},y_{n'}}
L$, $z: S \to L$ the induced map, $S_n = \sigma^n(S)$, $z_n = z | S_n$.

We have to show that $S_n$ has total dimension $0$.  Now $S$ is a
well-mixed $L$-algebra, and $\sigma^{n'}(S) \subset L$.  By assumption,
$S$ has total dimension $\leq n$.  We are reduced to showing:
<!-- end head-52 -->
<!-- head-53: body_md -->
Let $L$ be an inversive difference field,
 $S$ a finitely generated well-mixed difference $L$-algebra, with
 $\sigma^{n'}(S) \subset L$.  Assume $S$ has total dimension $ n < n'$. 
 Then $\sigma^n(S) $ has total dimension $0$.
<!-- end head-53 -->
<!-- cor-15: body_md -->
\label{trans-mult-0} A difference scheme $X$ has transformal multiplicity $\leq n$ iff
  $X \to B_{n+1}X $ has total dimension $\leq n$.
<!-- end cor-15 -->
<!-- head-54: body_md -->
It suffices to show that if $n<n'$ and
$X \to B_{n'}(X)$ has total dimension $\leq n$, then so does 
$X \to B_{n'+1}(X)$.   Let $k$ be a difference field, $y$ an $k$-valued point
of $B_{n'+1}$.  In terms of local rings, we have 
$R \supset \sigma^{n'}(R) \supset \sigma^{n'+1}(R)$, and $z: \sigma^{n'+1}(R) \to k$.
We have to show that $S = R {\otimes} _{\sigma^{n'+1}(R),z}  k$ has total dimension $\leq n$.
Let $(h,D,L)$ be as in the definition of total dimension.  
Let $S_m$ denote the image of $\sigma^m(R) {\otimes} _{\sigma^{n'+1}(R),z} k$ in $S$.

Observe in general that if $ X \to_f Y$ has relative total dimension $\leq n$, then 
so does the induced map $BX \to BY$.  Indeed, by Remark \ref{obviousmonotonicity},
the pullback $f^{-1}BY \to BY$ has total dimension $\leq n$, and $BX$ is a 
subscheme of $f^{-1}BY$, so \ref{obviousmonotonicity} applies again.  In 
particular, as  $X \to B_{n+1}X$ has total dimension $\leq n$, so does 
$B_{n'-n}X \to B_{n'+1}X$ .

By  lemma \ref{trans-mult-n},  $\sigma^n(\sigma^{n'-n}R {\otimes} _{\sigma^{n'+1}(R),z}  k)$ 
has total dimension $0$.  Thus $h(S_{n'})$ is finite dimensional over
$k$, so it is a difference subfield of the domain $D$, call it $k'$.   So
$h(\sigma^{n'}(R)) \subset k'$.  As $X \to B_{n'}(X)$ has total dimension $\leq n$,
$h(R)$ is contained in a field $F$ of $k'$-transcendence degree $\leq n$.
But $[k':k]< \infty$, so  $tr. deg._{k}(F) = tr. deg_{k'} (F) \leq n$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-54 -->
<!-- lem-37: body_md -->
\label{rm2} If $X$ is algebraically integral,of finite type over
a field $K$, then
the   $X_n$ stabilize as subschemes of $X$:  for some $n$, $X_n = X_{n+1} = \ldots$.
<!-- end lem-37 -->
<!-- head-55: body_md -->
This reduces to the affine case by taking an open affine cover; there it follows
from Corollary \ref{rm1}.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-55 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a difference ring.  A well-mixed ideal $I$ is {\em $\sigma$-primary} if
 whenever $a,b \in R$ and $ab \in I$, either $a \in I$ or $b^{\sigma^n} \in I$ for some $n \in \hbox{\msbmten N}[\sigma]$.
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- lem-38: body_md -->
\label{primary}  Let $I$ be a well-mixed ideal, and let $P =    \sqrt[\sigma]{I}$, and 
$R_P$   the localization of $R$ outside $P$.  Let $\iota: R \to R_P$ be the natural map.
The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $I$ is $\sigma$-primary
  \item $P$ is a transformal prime, and $I$ is   $P$-$\sigma$-primary
  \item  $P$ is a transformal prime, and  $I =\iota {^{-1}} (I')$  for some well-mixed ideal $I'$ of $R_P$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-38 -->
<!-- head-56: body_md -->
Since $I$ is a well-mixed ideal, $   \sqrt[\sigma]{I}$ is a perfect ideal (Lemma \ref{well-mixed1}.)
 If $I$ is $\sigma$-primary, then $P$ is a prime ideal, hence a transformal prime.  Thus
 (1) implies (2).  Assume (2).  Let $I' = \{a/b: a \in I, b \notin P\}$.  This is a well-mixed
 ideal of $R'$:  if $(a/b)(a'/b') \in I'$, then $(a/b)(a'/b') = a''/b''$ with $a'' \in I, b'' \notin P$.
 So $aa'b''=a''bb'$ in $R'$; upon multipliying denominators and numerators by an 
 appropriate element outside $P$, we may assume $aa'b''=a''bb' $ in $R$.  As $I$ is $P$-primary, and $a'' \in I$, we have $aa' \in I$; as $I$ is well-mixed,  $a^\sigma a' \in I$. 
 Now $(a/b)^\sigma (a'/b') = (a^\sigma a') / (b^\sigma b') \in I'$.  So $I'$ is well-mixed.  We have $I \subseteq \iota {^{-1}} (I')$, and if $a/1 \in I'$, then $a = a'/b$ for some $a' \in I$, $b \notin P$,
 so $(ab-a')b'=0$ for some $b' \notin P$, thus $ab-a' \in I$, so $ab \in I$, so $a \in I$.  This proves (3).  Now assume (3).  If $ab \in I$, and $b \notin P$, 
 then $\iota(b)$ is invertible; so $a/1 \in I'$, thus $a \in I$.    \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-56 -->
<!-- lem-39: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a finitely generated difference $k$-algebra, $k$ a difference field.
                                          
  Then there is no strictly increasing chain
 of    algebraically radical
 $\sigma$-primary well-mixed ideals.
<!-- end lem-39 -->
<!-- head-57: body_md -->
Suppose $I_1 \subset I_2 \subset \ldots \subset P$ is such a chain.  Let $P_k =    \sqrt[\sigma]{I_k}$.  Then $P_1 \subseteq P_2 \subseteq \ldots$, so by Ritt-Raudenbush 
  the $P_k$
 are eventually equal, and we may assume $   \sqrt[\sigma]{I_k}=P$.  Let $I = \cup_k I_k$.
 If $b \in R \setminus P$, $R' =  R[b {^{-1}}]_\sigma$, $I_k' = I_k R[b {^{-1}}]_\sigma$, then the $I_k'$
 form a strictly ascending chain, by Lemma \ref{primary} (3).  Thus, replacing $R$ by 
 an appropriate $R'$ using Lemma \ref{noether-2}, we may assume $I = \cup_k I_k$ is finitely  generated;
but it follows that $I=I_k$ for large enough $k$, a contradiction.   \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-57 -->
<!-- notation-5: body_md -->
When $K$  is a valued field, ${\cal O}_K,{\cal M}_K, {{\, \rm val \,}}(K),K_{{\rm res \,}}$
will denote
 the valuation ring, maximal ideal;  
 value group, residue field  of $K$; but we will often denote 
$R={\cal O}_K, M = {\cal M}_K, \bar{K} = K_{{\rm res \,}},  \Gamma=  {{\, \rm val \,}}(K)$.
<!-- end notation-5 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{tvr-def}
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item A transformal valuation ring  (domain) is a valuation ring $R$ that is also a difference ring,
  such that $\sigma(M) \subset M$ (and $\sigma$ injective.)

\item The valuation $v$
 will be said to be  $m$-increasing
 (resp. strictly increasing)
 if  for all $a \in R$ with $v(a)>0 $, $ v(\sigma(a)) \geq m \cdot v(a)$
  (resp. $v(\sigma(a))>v(a)$).  It is $\omega$-increasing if $m$-increasing for all $m$.

 \item A weakly
transformal valued field is an octuple $(K,R,M,\sigma,\Gamma,\bar{K},{\, \rm val \,},{\rm res \,})$ such that $(R,M,\sigma)$ is a transformal valuation
ring, $K$ is the field of fractions of $R$, $res:  K \to \bar{K}$ is the residue map, $val:  K^* \to \Gamma = G_m(K)/G_m(R)$
is the valuation map.  
\footnote{$G_m(R)$ is the group of invertible elements of $R$.}
We will also apply the term to parts of the data.  If $\sigma$ extends to an endomorphism of $K$, we
denote it too by $\sigma$, and we say that $K$ is a transformal valued field.  



\item  Assume given a distinguished  $t \in R $,
or at least a distinguished $\tau \in {\, \rm val \,}(R)$ ($\tau = {\, \rm val \,}(t)$). Let 
$$\Delta =    \{v \in {\, \rm val \,}(K):  -\tau < nv < \tau, \ n=1,2,\ldots \} $$

Write $a << b$ if $ma <b$ for all $m \in \hbox{\msbmten N}$.
    $K$  has {\em   transformal ramification dimension $rk_{ram}(K) = r$} (over
$\tau$)
if $r$ is the length of a maximal chain $v_0,\ldots,v_r \in {\, \rm val \,}(R)$ with
$0 = v_0 << v_1 << \ldots << v_r << \tau $.  When $K$ is $\omega$-
increasing, 
$rk_{ram}(K) \leq  {\rm dim \, } _{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} (\hbox{\msbmten Q} {\otimes} \Delta)$.  
(In   transformal dimension one, equality holds; cf \ref{vt1c}.)  When $K$ extends $k(t)_\sigma$,
taking ${\, \rm val \,}(t)$ distinguished, we define 
the {\em valuative rank} ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(K/k(t)_\sigma)$ of $K$ over $k(t)_\sigma$ to be $rk_{ram}(K) + tr. deg._k \bar{K}$.  
   

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- notation-6: body_md -->
\  \label{not-moving}
<!-- end notation-6 -->
<!-- lem-40: body_md -->
\label{tvrl} Let $(K,R,M,\sigma,\Gamma,\bar{K},val)$ be a weakly transformal valued field.  \begin{enumerate}

\item $\sigma^{-1}(M) = M$.  \ $\sigma(M) = M \cap \sigma(R)$.  If $K$ is $1$-increasing,
then every ideal of $R$ is a well-mixed difference ideal.   

\item There exists a unique difference field structure on $\bar{K}$, such that the residue map $R \to \bar{K}$ is a morphism
 of difference rings.    

\item There exits a convex subgroup $\Gamma'$ of $\Gamma$ and a homomorphism $\sigma_{\Gamma}:  \Gamma' \to \Gamma$ of ordered
Abelian groups, such $val(a) \in \Gamma'$ and $\sigma_{\Gamma}(val (a)) = val(\sigma (a))$ when $a \in R$, $ \sigma(a) \neq 0$.

If the valuation is $k$-increasing, then $k v \leq \sigma_{\Gamma}(v)$ for $v \in \Gamma, v \geq 0$.     

  \item Let $L$ be a subfield of $K$.  Then $\sigma(L^a \cap R) \subset (\sigma(L \cap R))^a$.  (where $S^a$ denotes the algebraic
closure of the field of fractions of $S$.)    

\item If $L$ is a subfield of $K$, and $\sigma( L \cap R) \subset L^a$, then $L^a \cap R$ is a difference subring of $R$.    

\item Let $\Delta$ be a convex subgroup of $\Gamma$ with ${\sigma_\Gamma}^{-1}( \Delta) \subset \Delta$.  (An automatic condition
  for    $1$-increasing valuations.)  Let $\widehat{v}$ be the valuation $ val(a) + \Delta$; with value group $\Gamma/\Delta$, residue field
  $\widehat{K}$.  Then a weakly transformal valued field structure is induced on $\widehat{K}$, with residue field $\bar{K}$, value
  group $\Delta$.    

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-40 -->
<!-- lem-41: body_md -->
\label{hensel-alg} Let $L^h$ be the Henselization of $L$ as a valued field.  The endomorphism $\sigma$ of $L$ 
lifts uniquely to a valued field endomorphism of  $L^h$.  If $L$ is $\omega$-increasing, so is $L^h$.
<!-- end lem-41 -->
<!-- head-58: body_md -->
$\sigma: L \to \sigma(L)$ is an isomorphism of valued fields; by the universal property of the
Henselization, for any Henselian valued field $M$ containing $\sigma(L)$, $\sigma$ extends uniquely to 
an embedding $L^h \to M$; in particular, with $M=L^h$, $\sigma$ extends to $\sigma: L^h \to L^h$.  The property of being $\omega$-increasing 
depends on the value group, which does not change. \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-58 -->
<!-- lem-42: body_md -->
\label{vt1}   Let  $L$ be                                                      
an extension of $F(t)_\sigma$ of finite transcendence degree. 
                                        
Then 
the value group ${\, \rm val \,} (L^a)$  of $L^a$ is isomorphic to $\Q-si$, as an ordered
  $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module.  Let $K \leq L$ be a difference subfield, nontrivially valued. Then
 ${\, \rm val \,}(K)$ is cofinal in ${\, \rm val \,}(L)$.  
   ${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)/{\, \rm val \,}(K^a)$ is a principal, torsion
$\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$-module.
<!-- end lem-42 -->
<!-- head-59: body_md -->
Pick $t \in K$, ${\, \rm val \,}(t)>0$.  Since $tr. deg. _{F(t)_\sigma} L < \infty$, ${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)/ {\, \rm val \,}({F(t)_\sigma}^a)$ is a finite-dimensional $\hbox{\msbmten Q}$-space.  Thus ${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)$ is a   finitely generated   $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$-module.   Since $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$ is a principal ideal domain,
and ${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)$ is torsion free,  
${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)$ is a free  $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$-module.  Now the quotient ${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)/ {\, \rm val \,}({F(t)_\sigma}^a)$ is finite-dimensional,
so the rank of ${\, \rm val \,}(L^a)$ must equal one.  Let $h:  \Q-si \to {\, \rm val \,} (L^a) $
be an isomorphism of  $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-modules.    Replacing $h$ by $-h$ if necessary,
 we may assume $h(1)>0$.  It follows that $h$ is order preserving.   
Any nonzero $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$ - submodule
of $\Q-si$  is cofinal, and co-torsion.  
 \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-59 -->
<!-- cor-16: body_md -->
\label{vt1c}   Let  $L$ be 
                                                     
                                                            
a transformal valued field extension of $F(t)_\sigma$ of finite transcendence degree. 
Then $rk_{ram}(L / F(t)_\sigma) = rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} ({\, \rm val \,}(L)/ {\, \rm val \,} F(t)_\sigma)$.
<!-- end cor-16 -->
<!-- lem-43: body_md -->
\label{vt2}  Let  $L$ be an $\omega$-increasing transformal valued field of 
finite transcendence degree over $F(t)_\sigma$.    Then the residue field ${\rm res \,} (L)$ of $L$ has finite transcendence degree over $F$.
<!-- end lem-43 -->
<!-- head-60: body_md -->
The residue field of $F(t)_\sigma$ is $F$ itself, and  $L$ has  finite transcendence degree over
$ F(t)_\sigma$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-60 -->
<!-- lem-44: body_md -->
\label{val-lem} Let 
 $K$ be an algebraically closed valued field, $L$ an extension of 
transcendence degree $1$.   Let $c \in L \setminus K$.  Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item  ${\rm res \,}(K) \neq {\rm res \,}(L)$ or  ${\, \rm val \,}(K) \neq {\, \rm val \,}(L)$
  \item  ${\rm res \,}(K(c)) \neq  {\rm res \,}(K)$ or  ${\, \rm val \,}(K(c)) \neq {\, \rm val \,}(K)$
  \item  $T(c/K) = \{val(c-b): b \in K \}$ has a maximal element. 
\end{enumerate} 
In particular, the third condition depends on $K,L$ alone and
not on the choice of $c$. 

$T(c/K)= {\, \rm val \,} K$ iff $L$ embeds into the completion $\widehat{K}$ as
a valued field.
<!-- end lem-44 -->
<!-- head-61: body_md -->
:    Let ${\cal O}_L$ be the valuation ring of $L$.
(1) implies (2) since if ${\rm res \,}(K(c))={\rm res \,}(K)$,
and ${\, \rm val \,} (K(c)) = {\, \rm val \,}(K)$, 
then ${\rm res \,}(K(c))$ is algebraically closed and ${\, \rm val \,}(K(c))$ is divisible;
so they cannot change under algebraic field extensions.  Now assume 
${\, \rm val \,}(K(c)) \neq {\, \rm val \,}(K)$.  Then ${\, \rm val \,} f(c) \notin {\, \rm val \,}(K)$ 
 for some $f \in K[X]$.    Splitting $f$ into linear factors, wee see that 
we can take it to be linear.  So ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b) \notin {\, \rm val \,}(K)$ for some $b \in K$.
It follows that ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b') \leq {\, \rm val \,}(c-b)$ for all $b' \in K$.  (Otherwise
${\, \rm val \,}(c-b)={\, \rm val \,}(b-b')$.)  Next suppose ${\, \rm val \,}(K(c)) = {\, \rm val \,}(K)$, but
 ${\rm res \,} f(c) \notin {\rm res \,} (K)$ for some $f \in K[X]$ with $f(c) \in {\cal O}_L$.  
Taking into account ${\, \rm val \,} (K(c)) = {\, \rm val \,}(K)$, we can split $f$ into linear
factors $f_i$ such that each $f_i(c) \in {\cal O}_L$.  Thus $ac-b \in {\cal O}_L$,
${\rm res \,}(ac-b) \notin {\rm res \,}(K) $ for some $a,b \in K$.  It follows that
${\, \rm val \,}(ac-b') \leq 0$ for all $b' \in K$.  So ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b/a)   \geq {\, \rm val \,}(c-b'')$
for all $b'' \in K$.  This proves that (2) implies (3).   

Now assume (3): ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b) \geq {\, \rm val \,}(c-b')$
for all $b' \in K$.  If ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b) \notin {\, \rm val \,}(K)$, (2) holds.  If ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b) = {\, \rm val \,}(d)$,
$d \in K$, then $(c-b)/d \in {\cal O}_L$, and ${\, \rm val \,}((c-b)/d-d') \leq 0$ for all $d'$;
so ${\rm res \,}((c-b)/d ) \notin {\rm res \,}(K)$.  Thus (1).  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-61 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
\label{vt4-e}  Let $F$ be a   field, $K=F(t_0,t_1,\ldots)^a$, valued over $F$ with $0<{\, \rm val \,}(t_0)<<{\, \rm val \,}(t_1)<< \cdots$.  
Let $K' = F(t_e,t_{e+1},\ldots)^a$, and let $c \in \widehat{K}  \setminus \widehat{K'}$.  Then 
$T(c/K') = \{ {\, \rm val \,}(c-b): b \in K' \}$ has a maximal element.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- head-62: body_md -->
If $T(c/K')$ is unbounded in ${\, \rm val \,}(K')$, then
$c \in \widehat{K'}$.  Otherwise, for all $b \in K'$, 
${\, \rm val \,}(c-b) \leq \alpha$.  Find $c' \in K$ with ${\, \rm val \,}(c-c') > \alpha$.
Then $T(c'/K')  = T(c/K')$.  Now $K^a/(K')^a$ is generated (as an algebraically
closed field) by $e$ elements,
whose values are $\hbox{\msbmten Q}$-linearly independent over ${\, \rm val \,}(K')$.  Thus
  ${\, \rm val \,} K'(c') \neq {\, \rm val \,} K'$; so  \ref{val-lem} applies,
and shows $T(c'/K')$ has a maximal element.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-62 -->
<!-- lem-45: body_md -->
\label{val-ort}  Let 
 $K$ be an algebraically closed valued field, $L$ an extension of 
transcendence degree $1$, $c,d \in L \setminus K$.  Then  
$E(c/K)=E(d/K)$.
<!-- end lem-45 -->
<!-- head-63: body_md -->
If one of $T(c/K),T(d/K)$ has a last element, then by \ref{val-lem}
so does the other, and $E(c/K)=(0)=E(d/K)$.  Thus we may 
assume $T(c/K),T(d/K)$ have no last element, so that ${\, \rm val \,} K = {\, \rm val \,} L =: \Gamma$.
Further, since $E(c,K),E(d/K)$ are convex subgroups, one is contained in the other, so we may assume   that $E(c/K) \subseteq E :=E(d/K)$.
 
 
In case  $E  = \Gamma$,  , by the last statement of \ref{val-lem},  $L$ embeds   into  
$\widehat{K}$, and hence $E(c/K)=\Gamma$ too.

In general, let $\Gamma' = \Gamma / E $,
$r: \Gamma \to \Gamma'$ the quotient map,  and let ${\, \rm val \,}': L \to \Gamma'$
be the   valuation obtained by composition, ${\, \rm val \,}' = r \circ {\, \rm val \,}$.   Note that ${\, \rm val \,}'(L)={\, \rm val \,}'(K) = \Gamma'$.
Call the  residue fields $K',L'$.  Let
$T'(y/K) = \{val'(y-b): b \in K \}$. 

  If $E(c/K) \neq E(d/K)$, then
 $T'(c/K)$ has a last element.  (Indeed let $\gamma \in E(d/K) $
 with $\gamma > 0$ and $\gamma \notin E(c/K)$.  Then there
 exists $\alpha \in T(c/K)$ with $\alpha + \gamma \notin T(c/K)$.
 Let ${\alpha}'$ be the common image of $\alpha,\alpha+\gamma$
 in $\Gamma'$.  Then clearly $\alpha'$ is the greatest element of
 $T'(c/K)$.)  By \ref{val-lem}, $T'(d/K)$ has a greatest element too.
Effecting additive and multiplicative translations, we may assume   these greatest
elements are ${\, \rm val \,}'(c)=0,{\, \rm val \,}'(d)=0$.  Let $c',d'$ be the residues
of $c,d$.

Since  ${\, \rm val \,}'(L)={\, \rm val \,}'(K) = \Gamma'$, by \ref{val-lem} we must
have $K' \neq L'$.   We have an induced valuation  ${\, \rm val \,}'': L' \to E $,
${\, \rm val \,}'' ({\rm res \,}' (a) ) = {\, \rm val \,}(a)$ for $a$ with ${\, \rm val \,}(a) \in E $.  
Clearly $T''(c'/K') = \{{\, \rm val \,}''(c'-b': b' \in K') \} = E \cap  T(c/K)$, and
similarly for $d$; thus $E''(c'/K') = E(c/K), E''(d'/K') = E(d/K)$.  But
now $T''(d/K)$ is the entire value group $E(d/K)$, so by the special case of $E=\Gamma$ considered above we have 
$E''(c'/K') = E''(d'/K')$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-63 -->
<!-- notation-7: body_md -->
\label{calHnotation}  For a linear ordering $L$ and $X \subseteq L$, let ${\cal H}_L(X) = \{y: (\exists x \in X) (y \leq x)\}$
<!-- end notation-7 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
\label{vt1c2}  Let $M \subset \hbox{\msbmten R}[\sigma]$ be a $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module.     The nonzero convex subgroups form a single $\sigma$-orbit $\{E_n: n=1,2,\ldots\}$, in the sense that
$E_{n+1}$ is the convex hull of $\sigma(E_n)$; $E_n = \sigma^{-1}(E_{n+1}).$
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- head-64: body_md -->
Let $(0)=C_0 \subset C_1 \subset \ldots$
be the proper convex subgroups of $\hbox{\msbmten R}[\sigma]$ (with $\sigma^{-1}(C_{n+1})=C_n $).  Then for some $m$, 
 $M \cap C_{m+1}  \neq (0)$,   $M \cap C_{m}  = (0)$. 
So for $n \geq 0$,  $E_n = C_{n+m} \cap M$ are convex subgroups of $M$.
If $E$ is any proper convex subgroup of $M$, then the convex hull of $E$ in $\Z-si$
must be some $C_{n+m}$, and it follows that $E=E_n$.    \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-64 -->
<!-- cor-17: body_md -->
\label{vt1r1} Let $K'=K(c)^a, K''=K(d)^a$ be two 
valued field extensions of an algebraically closed valued field $K$,  with $E(c/K) \neq E(d/K)$.  Then $K',K''$ have a unique valued field
amalgam. 

We have 
$T(c/K'') = {\cal H} T(c/K)$ (where  ${\cal H}(X) = \{y: (\exists x \in X) (y \leq x)\}$ ).

In particular if ${\, \rm val \,} K'' = {\, \rm val \,} K$ then $T(c/K'')=T(c/K)$,
and $E(c/K'') = E(c/K)$.
<!-- end cor-17 -->
<!-- head-65: body_md -->
Assume $K',K''$ are embedded in $L = K'K''$.  Let
 $a \in K', b \in K''$.  Then $E(a/K) = E(c/K) \neq E(d/K) = E(b/K)$, so $T(a/K) \neq T(b/K)$.  One of $T(a/K),T(b/K)$ is bigger, say
$T(a/K) \subset T(b/K)$.  Find $e \in K$ with ${\, \rm val \,}(b-e) > T(a/K)$.
Then ${\, \rm val \,}(a-b) = {\, \rm val \,}(a-e)$.  This shows that the values of elements
$a-b$ are all determined.  In particular the values ${\, \rm val \,}(c-b)$
for $b \in K(d)$ are determined; this determines $tp(c/K'')$ and 
hence $tp(K'/K'')$.   

Moreover we see that
every element ${\, \rm val \,}(c-a)$ of $T(c/K'')$ either equals ${\, \rm val \,}(c-e)$
for some $e \in K$, so that it lies in $T(c/K)$, or else 
equals ${\, \rm val \,}(a-e) $ where ${\, \rm val \,}(c-e) > {\, \rm val \,}(a-e)$; so
in either case it lies in ${\cal H} T(c/K)$.  
\hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-65 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{vt1r3}  Let $L$ be a valued field extension of an algebraically closed valued field $K$.  
 Let $a_i \in L \setminus K$,   
$$T_i = T(a_i/K) = \{val(a_i -b): b \in K \} $$
Assume  that the convex subgroups 
 $$E_i = E(a_i/K)=  \{e \in {\, \rm val \,} K: e+T_i=T_i\}$$
 are distinct.  
   Then $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ are algebraically independent over $K$.
The valued field structure of $K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is uniquely determined
by the $T_i$.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- head-66: body_md -->
By assumption, $a_i \notin K^{alg}$. Use induction
on $n$.  Some
$E_i$ is nonzero; say  $E_1 \neq (0)$.  Let $K'  = K(a_1)^a$.  By \ref{val-lem},
${\, \rm val \,} K' = {\, \rm val \,} K$.  By \ref{val-ort}, $a_i,a_1$ are algebraically
independent over $K$ for $i \neq 1$.  By  \ref{vt1r1}, the type
of $(a_i,a_1)/K$ is determined, and 
$E(a_i/K') = E(a_i/K)$.  By induction, $a_2,\ldots,a_n$ are
independent over $K'$, and their type over $K'$ is determined.
The conclusion follows.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-66 -->
<!-- lem-46: body_md -->
\label{acf-acvf-comp}  
  
 Let $F \leq K_{1},K_{2}$ be algebraically  
  closed valued fields.  Assume $K_2$ can be embedded into $\widehat{F}$ over $F$;
  and that in any embedding of $K_1,K_2$ into a valued field extension $L$ of $F$, the images
  are linearly disjoint over $F$.  
   Then $K_{1},K_{2}$ are almost-orthogonal over
 $F$.
 
 In particular, if  $F \leq K_{1},K_{2} \leq \widehat{F}, $ then $K_{1},K_{2}$ are almost-orthogonal over
 $F$ if and only if  they are  linearly disjoint over $F$.
<!-- end lem-46 -->
<!-- head-67: body_md -->
We may assume here that $tr. deg. _{F }K_{1} < \infty$. 
 If $F \leq F' \leq K_1$ then the hypotheses hold for $F,F',K_2$ and then also
 for $F',K_1,F'K_2$; so using transitivity of almost orthogonality 
    the lemma reduces to the case 
    $tr. deg. _{F }K_{1} =1$.  Fix some embedding of $K_1,K_2$ into a valued field $L$.
    Let $a \in K_{1} \setminus F$.  
    Then $a \notin K_{2}$, by the linear disjointness assumption.
      Let $B$ be a $K_{2}$-definable ball
    with $a \in B$.  So $B = B_{\rho}(b)= \{y: {\, \rm val \,}(y-b) \geq \rho \}$,
    $\rho  \in {\, \rm val \,}(K_{2}), b \in K_{2}$.  
As $a \notin K_{2}$, $\rho < \infty$.
Since $b  \in \widehat{F}$
    and $\rho \in {\, \rm val \,}(\widehat{F}) = {\, \rm val \,}(F)$, there exists $b' \in F$
    with ${\, \rm val \,}(b-b')> \rho$.  So $B$ is $F$-definable.  Thus
    $tp(a/F)$ implies $a \in B$.  Since $B$ was arbitrary, and $K_{2}$ is 
    algebraically closed,  the formulas $x \in B$
    of this kind generate $tp(a/K_{2})$.  Thus
    $tp(a/F)$ implies $tp(a/K_{2})$.  So $F(a),K_{2}$ are almost 
    orthogonal over $F$. By Theorem 2.11 of \cite{HHM2}, $K_{1}
    ,K_{2}$ are almost-orthogonal over $F$.    
   \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-67 -->
<!-- lem-47: body_md -->
\label{domin-val} Let $K_0 \subset K_1 \subset  \cdots \subset K_n$ be algebraically closed valued fields, $K=\widehat{K_0}, L=\widehat{K_n}$.    Assume: 
${\, \rm val \,}(K_0)$ is cofinal in ${\, \rm val \,}(K_n)$; and for each $i$, $K_{i+1}/K_i$ is 
purely ramified, or purely inertial, or $K_{i+1} \subset \widehat{K_i}$.  Let  
${\bar{K}}$ be an immediate extension of $K$.    Then:
   $\bar{K},L$ are almost orthogonal over $K$, and $M=L {\bar{K}}$ is  an immediate extension of $L$.
<!-- end lem-47 -->
<!-- head-68: body_md -->
\def\L-{{L^{-}}} \def{\cal M}-{{M^{-}}}
(1) Let $\L- =\widehat{K_{n-1}} ,  \,  {\cal M}-   = \L-{\bar{K}}$.  We may 
assume inductively that $ \bar{K},\L- $ are almost orthogonal over $K$, and ${\cal M}-$  is  an immediate extension of $\L-$, hence of ${K_{n-1}}$.  We will show that ${\cal M}-,L$ are
are almost orthogonal over $\L-$, and $M$  is  an immediate extension of $L$.  
From this (1) follows by transitivity.  

If $K_n \subseteq \widehat{K_{n-1}}$, then $\L-=L$ and there is nothing to prove.  
Otherewise $K_n/K_{n-1}$ is  purely ramified, or purely inertial.  Since ${\cal M}-$
  is  an immediate extension of   ${K_{n-1}}$, it follows that
$\L- K_n / \L-$ is purely ramified, or purely inertial; for instance in the purely inertial case,
using $(K_{n-1})_{{\rm res \,}} = (\L-)_{{\rm res \,}}$ we have
$$tr. deg._{\L-} \L- K_n   \leq tr. deg._{K_{n-1}} K_n  =  tr.deg._{(K_{n-1})_{{\rm res \,}}} (K_n)_{{\rm res \,}} \leq 
tr.deg._{(\L-)_{{\rm res \,}}} (\L- K_n)_{{\rm res \,}}  $$
so the numbers are equal. 
This also shows that   $\L-K_n  $ is
almost orthogonal to ${\cal M}-$ over $\L-$.   By {Lemma \ref{complete-max}}, $L$ is 
almost orthogonal to ${\cal M}-$ over $\L-$, and
${\cal M}- L$ is an immediate extension of $L$.  But $M={\cal M}-L$.                 \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-68 -->
<!-- lem-48: body_md -->
\label{gauss} Let $k \leq K$ be   algebraically closed fields.  Let $v$ be a valuation of
$K/k$, $R$ the valuation ring.  Let $X$ be a quasi-projective scheme over $R$, with $X(K)$ and $X(k)$ finite.
Consider the residue homomorphism $R \to k$, and the induced map $r: X(R) \to X(k)$.
If $p \in X(k)$ and $r^{-1}(p)$ has $n$ distinct points, then $p$ has geometric multiplicity 
$\geq n$ on the scheme $X_0 = X {\otimes}_R k$.  More generally, this holds true if $r^{-1}(p)$
has $n$ points counted with multiplicities on $(X {\otimes}_R K) $.  If $X$ is flat over $R$ (or, is reduced and has no component lying over the special fiber of ${\rm Spec \, } R$) equality holds.
<!-- end lem-48 -->
<!-- head-69: body_md -->
Find an affine open subscheme containing the said $n$ points $q_1,\ldots,q_n$, and thus   reduce   to $X = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } A$, $A$ a finitely 
generated  $R$-algebra.   Let $B$ be the image  of $A$ in $A {\otimes}_R K$.     As $X$ is $0$-dimensional, $A {\otimes}_R K$ is a finite dimensional $K$-space, and so the finitely generated $R$-submodule $B$ is a free $R$-module of finite rank.   
  It follows that  $ {\rm dim \, } _k (A {\otimes}_R k) \geq 
 {\rm dim \, } _k  ( B {\otimes} _R k) =  {\rm dim \, } _K (B {\otimes} _R K)                       
=  {\rm dim \, } _K(A {\otimes}_R K)$.

If $X$ is flat over $R$,  then $A$ is a flat $R$ module, so $A \to A {\otimes}_R K$ is an injective map of modules, and hence $B \cong A$.

 \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-69 -->
<!-- example-5: body_md -->
Let $K$ be a transformal discrete valuation ring, with value group 
 $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$, and   residue field   $F(a)_\sigma$, where
  $g(a)=0$ for some difference polynomial $g$ over $F$ while $g'(a) \neq 0$.   Then  there exists a $1$-generated
  transformal discrete valuation ring over $F$, with the same value group and residue field.
<!-- end example-5 -->
<!-- example-6: body_md -->
\
<!-- end example-6 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{vt4}  Let $K=K^a$ be a transformal valued field with value group 
${\, \rm val \,}(K) \subset \Q-si$.  
Assume:  (*) for any $c \in K$,
$\{{\, \rm val \,}(c-b): b \in \sigma(K) \}$ has a greatest element.

Let $L$ be a valued difference field extension of $K$, with 
$  tr. deg._K(L) < \infty$, ${\, \rm val \,}(L)={\, \rm val \,}(K)$,
and $L_{{\rm res \,}} = K_{{\rm res \,}}$.  Then $\widehat{L} =  \widehat{K}$.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- head-70: body_md -->
Let $a \in L$; we will show that $a \in \widehat{K}$.  We may assume ${\, \rm val \,}(a)>0$.  Let
$a_n = \sigma^n(a)$, $C_n =  \{ \max(0,{\, \rm val \,}(a_n-b)): b \in K  \}$, $C=C_0$.
 Then $C_n$ is closed downwards in the non-negative elements ${\, \rm val \,}(K) $.
$C_n$ cannot have a maximal element, since
$L$ is an immediate extension of $K$.    
  
  If $C$ is unbounded,
then $a \in \widehat{K}$.  Suppose for contradiction that $C$ is
bounded.  We have $\Q-si = \hbox{\msbmten Q} v  \oplus \hbox{\msbmten Q} v^\sigma + \ldots$; let 
$E_m = \hbox{\msbmten Q} v \oplus \ldots \oplus \hbox{\msbmten Q} v^{\sigma^m}$. 
Let $m$ be least such that $C \leq E_m + c_0$ for some $c_0 \in C$ (here we write $X \leq Y$
if $(\forall x \in X)(\exists y \in Y) (x \leq y)$.)  
                                                                                                 
Since ${\, \rm val \,}(L)={\, \rm val \,}(K)$, dividing $a$ by an element of $K$ with value
$c_0$, we may assume                  
$C \leq E_m$; as $E_m$ is convex, we have $C \subset E_m$.  
Then $\sigma(C) \subset E_{m+1}$.  Let $H_1$ be the convex hull of $\sigma(C)$.

{\noindent \bf Claim } $E_m + H_1 = H_1$.
<!-- end head-70 -->
<!-- head-71: body_md -->
Let $0<e \in E_m$, $0<c \in C$.  Since $C \not \leq c+E_{m-1}$
                              
there exists $c' \in C$ , $l \in \hbox{\msbmten N}$ with $c' -c > e  / l$.  Then $\sigma(c'-c) > l (c'-c) > e$.
So $e+ \sigma(c) \leq \sigma(c')$.   


{\noindent \bf Claim } $H_1=C_{1}$
<!-- end head-71 -->
<!-- head-72: body_md -->
Let $c_1<c_2<\ldots$ be cofinal in $C$.  Let $b_n \in K$,  ${\, \rm val \,}(a-b_n) = c_n$; 
let $B_n = \{x: {\, \rm val \,}(x-b_n) \geq c_n \}$; $P = \cap _{n \in \hbox{\msbmten N}} B_n$;
$ {B_n}^\sigma = \{x: {\, \rm val \,}(x-\sigma(b_n)) \geq \sigma(c_n) \}$;
$P^\sigma = \cap_{n \in \hbox{\msbmten N}} {B_n}^\sigma$.
 
Then $P(K) = \emptyset$.  So $P^\sigma(K^\sigma) = \emptyset$.   
By the assumption (*) on $K/K^\sigma$, $P^\sigma(K) = \emptyset$.  Since
$a_1 \in P^\sigma$, it follows that there can be no $b \in K$
with ${\, \rm val \,}(b-a_1) > \sigma(C)$.  Thus $C_1 = H_1$.

Now $\sigma^n$ induces an isomorphism $(K,\sigma(K)) \to (\sigma^n(K),\sigma^{n+1}(K))$.
So the convex hull of 
$\sigma^n(C)$ is  $C_n$ for all $n$; $E_{m+n} + C_{n+1} = C_{n+1}$;
and $C_n \subset {\cal H}(E_{m+n})$ (\ref{calHnotation}).
   Thus the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{vt1r3}
are valid of the $C_m$.  

But now by \ref{vt1r3}, the elements $a_n$ must be
algebraically independent over $K$.  
This contradicts the assumption of finite transcendence degree. 
  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-72 -->
<!-- example-7: body_md -->
The composition of difference  polynomials extends to $F(t)_\sigma$, and by
continuity to the completion $L$ of $F(t)_\sigma$. 
 By \ref{vt4}, difference polynomials with nonzero linear term have a left compositional  inverse in $L$.
<!-- end example-7 -->
<!-- lem-49: body_md -->
\label{hensel-c}  Let $K$ be a  complete, algebraically Henselian transformal valued field over $F$, with value group 
${\, \rm val \,}(K) \subset \Q-si$.  Let ${f} \in {\cal O}_K[X]_\sigma$ be a difference polynomial,
 ${f_\nu}  = \partial_{\nu} {f}$.  
Suppose  $a \in {\cal O}_K$, $v={\, \rm val \,} ({f}(a)) > 2 {\, \rm val \,} ( f_1(a)) =2v'$.   Then 
there exists $b \in K$, $f(b)=0$, ${\, \rm val \,}(a-b) \geq v-v'$.
<!-- end lem-49 -->
<!-- head-73: body_md -->
Let $e_0 = f(a)$.
We will find
$a_1 \in {\cal O}_K$, ${\, \rm val \,}(a-a_1) \geq v-v'$, ${\, \rm val \,} f(a_1) \geq  \sigma(v)$.  Since
${\, \rm val \,} ( f_1(a) - f_1(a_1)) \geq v-v' > v' = {\, \rm val \,} f_1(a)$, it follows that ${\, \rm val \,} f_1(a_1) = v'$.
 Iterating this we get a sequence
$a_n$, with $v_n =_{def} {\, \rm val \,} f(a_n) \geq \sigma(v_{n-1})$, and ${\, \rm val \,} (a_{n-1} - a_n) \geq v_n - v'$. 
As $K$ is complete, there exists a unique $b \in K $ such that the sequence $a_n$ converges to $b$;
by continuity, $f(b)=0$.  

To obtain $a_1$, write $a_1= a + re$, with $e=e_0 / f_1(a)$, and $r \in {\cal O}_K$ to be found.  
    Then 

$$f(a_1)=f(a+re) = e_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(a) (re)^i + \sum_{\nu} f_\nu(a) (re)^\nu$$

Here the $f_i$ are transformal derivatives, cf.     \ref{trans-der} 
 $\nu$ runs over indices $\geq \sigma$, while $i$ ranges over the nonzero finite indices.  Note
that ${\, \rm val \,}    f_\nu(a) (re)^\nu \geq {\, \rm val \,}(\sigma(e)) = \sigma(v)$.  Thus it suffices to find $r$ with 
$e_0+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(a) (re)^i =0$, or with $r$ a root of 
$$g(x)= 1+ x + f_2(a) (e^2/e_0) x^2 + \ldots + f_m(a) (e^{m}/e_0) x^m $$
(Divide through by $e_0$, noting  $f_1(a)(e/e_0) =1$.)
This (ordinary) polynomial has derivative 
$$g'(x) = 1 + 2f_2(a)(e^2/e_0)x + \ldots $$
Now   for $k \geq 2$, ${\, \rm val \,} (e^k / e_0) = k (v-v') -v  
  \geq 2(v-v') - v = v-2v' > 0$.  Thus ${\rm res \,} g'$ is a nonzero constant polynomial.  By the
ordinary Hensel lemma, there exists $r \in {\cal O}_K$ with $g(r)=0$, near any $c \in {\cal O}_K$ with ${\, \rm val \,} g(c) > 0$.
Letting $c = -1$                     
 we see that there  exists $r \in {\cal O}_K$ with $g(r)=0$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-73 -->
<!-- cor-18: body_md -->
\label{res-lift-lem-0}  Let $K =K^a  \leq L $ be transformal valued
fields, with $L$   transformally henselian.  Let 
 ${f} \in K_{{\rm res \,}}[X]_\sigma$ be a difference polynomial
of order $r$, ${f}' = \partial_1 {f}$. 
  Let ${\bar{a}} \in L_{{\rm res \,}}$, ${f}({\bar{a}})=0$, ${f}'({\bar{a}}) \neq 0$,   
$tr.deg._{K_{{\rm res \,}}} K_{{\rm res \,}}({\bar{a}}) = r$.
Then   there exists a purely inertial extension $K'=K(b)_\sigma$ of $K$,
$K' \leq L$, ${\bar{a}} \in {\rm res \,}(K')$.
<!-- end cor-18 -->
<!-- head-74: body_md -->
Pick any $a \in {\cal O}_L$ with ${\rm res \,}(a)={\bar{a}}$, and also lift $f$ to ${\cal O}_K[X]_\sigma$.  Then ${\, \rm val \,} f(a) > 0$,
${\, \rm val \,} f'(a) = 0$, so by the transformal Hensel property (cf. \ref{hensel-c})  there exists $b \in {\cal O}_K$ with $f(b)=0$, ${\rm res \,}(b)= {\bar{a}}$.  Clearly $K'=K(b)_\sigma$
is purely inertial over $K$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-74 -->
<!-- cor-19: body_md -->
\label{res-lift-lem}  Let $K$ be an $\omega$-increasing   transformally henselian  valued field over $F$.
  Let ${\bar{a}} \in K_{{\rm res \,}}$, ${f}({\bar{a}})=0$, ${f}'({\bar{a}}) \neq 0$, ${f} \in F[X]_\sigma$ a difference polynomial, ${f}' = \partial_1 {f}$.  
Then $F({\bar{a}})_\sigma$ lifts to $K$:  there exists a subfield $F(b)_\sigma$ of $K$ such that the residue map 
restricts to an isomorphism $F(b)_\sigma \to F({\bar{a}})_\sigma$ (of difference $F$-algebras.)
<!-- end cor-19 -->
<!-- head-75: body_md -->
Pick any $a \in {\cal O}_K$ with ${\rm res \,}(a)={\bar{a}}$, and also lift $f$ to ${\cal O}_K[X]_\sigma$.  Then ${\, \rm val \,} f(a) > 0$,
${\, \rm val \,} f'(a) = 0$, so by \ref{hensel-c}, there exists $b \in {\cal O}_K$ with $f(b)=0$, ${\rm res \,}(b)= {\bar{a}}$.  The difference
field $ F(b)_\sigma$ has finite transcendence degree $m$ over $F$, and hence contained in $F'$; 
thus it is trivially valued, so the residue map is injective on $F(b)_\sigma$.  since ${\rm res \,}(b) = {\bar{a}}$,
it   carries $ F(b)_\sigma$ into and onto $F({\bar{a}})_\sigma$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-75 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{res-lift}  Let $K$ be a perfect $\omega$-increasing   transformally henselian  valued field
over a  difference field $F$.
 
Assume $F^{inv} \subset F^a$, and $K_{{\rm res \,}}$ has transformal transcendence degree $0$ over $F$.  Then
  ${\rm res \,}: F' \to K_{res}$ is surjective.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- head-76: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{inv-fin}, $(F')^{inv} \subset (F')^a$; and clearly $F'$ is perfect.
We may   assume $F'=F$, and show that ${\rm res \,}(K)=F$.       Suppose
$K_{{\rm res \,}} \neq F$.  In characteristic $0$, choose a difference polynomial $f \in F[X]_\sigma$ of smallest possible
transformal order and degree, and  ${\bar{a}} \in K_{{\rm res \,}}$
with $f({\bar{a}})=0$.  If $f \in F[X^\sigma]_\sigma$, then replacing ${\bar{a}}$ by $\sigma({\bar{a}})$ we may
lower the degree of $f$; unless $\sigma({\bar{a}}) \in F$.  But in this case, ${\bar{a}} \in F^a$,
so the order of $f$ must be $0$, so $f \in F[X^\sigma]$ is impossible.  Thus $f \notin F[X^\sigma]$.
It follows that $f' \neq 0$ and $f'$ has smaller order or degree.  So the hypothesis
of \ref{res-lift-lem} is met, and we can increase $F'$.

In positive characteristic, this may not be the case, because of polynomials such as $x^\sigma - x^p$.  
However, after replacing $\sigma$ by $\tau = \sigma(x^{1/p^m})$ for large enough $m$, it is possible to 
find such an ${\bar{a}}$ for $\tau$, lowering the degree of $f$ further.  Assuming the residue field of finite total dimension, this permits lifting the residue field; we may then   return from $\tau$ to $\sigma$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-76 -->
<!-- rem-6: body_md -->
\
<!-- end rem-6 -->
<!-- example-8: body_md -->
\  \label{res-lift-ex}
<!-- end example-8 -->
<!-- lem-50: body_md -->
\label{char-comp} Let $L=L^a$ be a transformal valued field over $F=F^{inv}$, 
with value group $\subset \hbox{\msbmten Q}_\sigma$.    Assume $L$ is complete.  Then the following conditions 
are equivalent:  \begin{enumerate}
  \item $L=\widehat{L_0}$ for some transformal valued field $L_0$ of transformal dimension $1$ over $F$.
  \item Whenever $L' = (L')^a  \leq L$ is complete with the same value group and
residue field,   $L'=L$.
  \item $L \simeq \widehat{K}$, where $K = (L_{{\rm res \,}}(t)_\sigma)^a$.  
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-50 -->
<!-- head-77: body_md -->
Assume(1), and let $L'$ be as in (2).  By \ref{vt2},  $L$ has value group $\hbox{\msbmten Q}_\sigma$, and   $L_{{\rm res \,}}$ has
transformal transcendence degree $0$ over $F$.  So $L_{{\rm res \,}}$ is inversive.  

Let $t \in L'$ be such that ${\, \rm val \,}(t)$ generates ${\, \rm val \,}(L)$ as a $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$-module.
By \ref{res-lift}, $L_{\rm res \,}$ lifts to a trivially valued difference subfield $F'$ of $L'$.
Let $K = (F'(t)_\sigma)^a$.  Then $K_{{\rm res \,}} =   L_{{\rm res \,}}$, and ${\, \rm val \,}(K) = {\, \rm val \,}(L)$.  

We have ${\, \rm val \,}(K) \neq {\, \rm val \,}(K^\sigma)$, while $tr. deg._{\sigma(K)} K = 1$.  By
\ref{val-lem}, the  hypothesis (*) of \ref{vt4} holds for $K$.  Thus by 
\ref{vt4}, $L =  \widehat{K}$.  Since $\widehat{K} \leq L' \leq L$, we have also $L'=L$.  
This proves (2).  

The same proof   shows that $K$ embeds into $L$; so assuming (2), we conclude (3),
using the assumption of (2) in place of \ref{vt4}.

(3) implies (1) trivially.
  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-77 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{lift-val}    Let $L=L^a$ be a transformal valued field of transformal dimension $1$ over an inversive difference
field $F=L_{res}$; with value group $\Q-si$. 
Let $F < K=K^a \leq \widehat{L}$.       Then  
 there exists a difference field $K' \leq \widehat{L}$,   with \begin{enumerate}
  \item $K \leq K'$, and $K'/K$ is purely ramified.
  \item With $e =  rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}(L)/{\, \rm val \,}(K')$, $\sigma^e \widehat{L} = \widehat{K'}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- head-78: body_md -->
Let $K'$ be a maximal   purely ramified difference field extension of $K$ within $\widehat{L}$.  Then $K' = (K')^{a}$.

By  \ref{char-comp}, $\widehat{L} = \widehat { F(t)_\sigma^a}$ for some $t$.  Let $e = rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}(L) / {\, \rm val \,}(K')$.  
Then there exists $s \in K'$, ${\, \rm val \,}(s) >0$, ${\, \rm val \,}(s) \in H_{e+1}$.  Fix $N \geq e+1$ for a moment.  
 Let $t_n = \sigma^n(t), s_m = \sigma^m(s)$, 
$\bar{t_n} =\, {\rm RES} \,_N(t_n)$, $\bar{s_n} = \, {\rm RES} \,_N (s)$.  

We saw that $tr. deg._F \, {\rm RES} \,_{N} (L) = N$.   Thus
 $\bar{t_0},\ldots,\bar{t_e},\bar{s_0},\ldots,\bar{s}_{N-e-1}$
are algebraically dependent over $F$.   Since $s \in H_{e+1}$, 
$\bar{s_0},\ldots,\bar{s}_{N-e-1}$ are algebraically independent over $F$, using the valuation ${\, \rm val \,}^*_e$     .  Let $m$ be maximal such that 
 $ \bar{t_m},\ldots,\bar{t_e},\bar{s_0},\ldots,\bar{s}_{N-e-1}$ are algebraically dependent over $F$.  
 
Write $f( \bar{t_m},\ldots,\bar{t_e},\bar{s_0},\ldots,\bar{s}_{N-e-1})   =0$, $f \in F[ X_m,\ldots,X_e,\bar{s_0},\ldots,\bar{s}_{N-e-1}]$ of minimal $X_m$- degree.


 We now argue that $m=e$. Lift $f$ to $ f( X_m,\ldots,X_e,s_0,\ldots,s_{N-e-1}) \in {\cal O}_L [X_m]_\sigma$,   viewed  as a difference polynomial in $X_m$ ( with coefficients involving the $s_i$, and $X_{m+j} =  (X_m)^{\sigma^j}$.)
  In characteristic $0$,
let $f'$ be the (first) derivative of $f$ with respect to $X_m$; then $f' \neq 0$, and so by minimality of $f$,
 $RES_N f'( \bar{t_m},\ldots,\bar{t_e})  \neq 0$, i.e. ${\, \rm val \,}  f'( t_m,\ldots,t_e) \in H_N$.  
By \ref{hensel-c}, applied to the element $t_m$, there exists $b \in \widehat{L}$,
 ${\, \rm val \,}(t_m -b) > H_{N}$, $f( b,\ldots,\sigma^{e-m}(b),s_0,\ldots,s_{N-e-1}) = 0$.  Let $L' = K'(b)_\sigma$.  
Clearly $tr. deg._K L' \leq e-m$,
while $rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}(L') / {\, \rm val \,}(K') \geq e-m$ 
(since ${\, \rm val \,}(\sigma^i(b))={\, \rm val \,}(t_{m+i})$, and  ${\, \rm val \,}(t_m) << {\, \rm val \,}(t_{m+1}) << \ldots << {\, \rm val \,}(t_{e-1}) << {\, \rm val \,}(c)$
for any $c \in K'$, ${\, \rm val \,}(c) > 0$.)  
However 
$rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}(L') / {\, \rm val \,}(K') \leq tr. deg._{K'} L' $, so 
these numbers are equal, and $L'/K'$ is purely ramified, of transcendence degree $m-e$.
  But  $K'$ is a maximal purely ramified extension; so $K'=L'$, and   $m=e$.

In characteristic $p$, we first replace $\sigma$ by $\sigma \circ \phi^{-l}$ where $\phi(x)=x^{p}$,
reduce the equation if it is now a $p$'th power, till $t_{m}$ occurs with an exponent
that is not a power of $p$.   We then use the above argument.  So $m=e$ in any
characteristic.  

 Thus  $\bar{t_{e}} \in \, {\rm RES} \,_{N}(K')$ (since this residue field is algebraically
closed).  So for some $b_N \in K'$, ${\, \rm val \,}(t_{e }-b_N ) > H_{N }(L)$.  Now letting $N \to \infty$,
 we see that $t_e \in \widehat{K'}$.   Let $K'' = F(t_e)^a_\sigma $;  then
 $  \sigma^e \widehat{L} = \widehat{K''}  \subset \widehat{K'}$,
and it remains to show equality.   Note that ${\, \rm val \,}(K'')  = \hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma] {\, \rm val \,}(t_e) = {\, \rm val \,} (K')$, and
${\rm res \,}(K'') = F = {\rm res \,}(K')$.   Thus $K'/K''$ is immediate, so for any $c \in K'$, 
$T(c) = \{{\, \rm val \,}(c-b): b \in K'' \}$ can have no maximum value (\ref{val-lem}).  But by \ref{vt4-e}, 
for any $c \in \widehat{L} \setminus \widehat{K''}$, $T(c)$ does have a maximal element.
Thus $K'=K''$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-78 -->
<!-- cor-20: body_md -->
\label{char-comp-cor}  If $L$ satisfies \ref{char-comp} (1)-(3), and $K$ is an algebraically closed, complete   difference
 subfield of $L$, $K_{{\rm res \,}}=L_{{\rm res \,}}$, then either $K$ is trivially valued or $K$ satisfies the same conditions.
<!-- end cor-20 -->
<!-- head-79: body_md -->
By \ref{res-lift}, we may assume $L,K$ are transformally valued fields over $F$, $F=K_{{\rm res \,}}=L_{{\rm res \,}}$.    Let $K'$
be as in \ref{lift-val}.  Then $K'/K$ is purely ramified, of finite transcendence degree $r$; there
exist  therefore $K_0 \leq K$,$K'_0 \leq K'$, $tr. deg._F (K_0)$ finite, $tr. deg. _{K_0} (K'_0) = r = rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}(K'_0)/{\, \rm val \,}(K_0)$,
 $K'=K K'_0$.  We can choose ${K_0}$ algebraically closed, and
with value group equal to ${\, \rm val \,}(K)$.   So $\widehat{K_0}   \leq \widehat{K'_0} \leq \widehat{K'}$.   $\widehat{K'}$ is isomorphic (by \ref{char-comp} (1 $\to$ 3)) to $L$, so it   satisfies
\ref{char-comp} (1)-(3); by (2), since $\widehat{K'_0} $ is a complete difference subfield with the same
value group and residue field, $ \widehat{K'} =  \widehat{K'_0}$.  Thus
$\widehat{K_0}   \leq K \leq \widehat{K'} = \widehat{K'_0}$.
If $c \in \widehat{K'} \setminus \widehat{K_0}$, as $K'_0/K_0$ is purely ramified, and as in the proof of 
\ref{vt4-e}, $K_0(c)/K_0$ is also purely ramified.  In particular if $c \in K \setminus \widehat{K_0}$ then
${\, \rm val \,} (c) \notin K_0$; but we chose ${\, \rm val \,}(K_0) = {\, \rm val \,}(K)$.  Thus $K=\widehat{K_0}$. 
Now $\widehat{K_0}$
satisfies  \ref{char-comp} (1). 
 \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-79 -->
<!-- cor-21: body_md -->
\label{vrk} Let $K$ be an $\omega$-increasing transformal valued field of transformal dimension $1$ over an inversive
 difference field $F$, with value group $\hbox{\msbmten Q}_\sigma$.   Let $L=L^a$ be a difference field extension of $K$ of
 finite transcendence degree.     Then the following are equivalent:  
\begin{enumerate}
  \item ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}} (L/K) \leq e$
  \item There exist  difference fields  $K \leq K_r \leq \widehat{K}$,
and  $K_r \leq K_1 \leq K_2 \leq   \widehat{L}$,  with: \begin{enumerate}
  \item $tr.deg._K K_r \leq tr. deg._F K_{{\rm res \,}}$                           
  \item  $tr. deg._{K_r} K_1  =  tr.deg._{K_{{\rm res \,}}} L_{{\rm res \,}} = e_{{\rm res \,}}$
  \item  $tr. deg._{K_1} K_2 = rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}(K_2)/{\, \rm val \,}(K_1)  = e_1$
  \item $\widehat{K_2} = \widehat{L}^{\sigma^{e_2}}$
  \item $e_{{\rm res \,}}+e_1 +e_2 \leq e$
\end{enumerate}

 
  \item There exists a difference field $K'$, $ \widehat{K} \leq K' \leq  \widehat{L}$, 
$tr.deg._{\widehat{K}} K' + e_2 \leq e$, $\widehat{K'} = \widehat{L}^{\sigma^{e_2}}$.

\item  There exist difference fields $K',M $, $\widehat{K} \leq K', \widehat{K'} \leq M, \widehat{M} = \widehat{L}$, with
$tr.deg._{\widehat{K}} K' + tr. deg._{\widehat{K'}}(M) \leq e$.
\end{enumerate}


Thus, if ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K)< \infty$, there exists a chain 
of difference subfields $K = M_0 \leq M_1 \leq \cdots \leq M_5=\widehat{L}$
such that  $M_{i+1} = \widehat{M_i}$ for even $i<5$, while for odd $i<5$
  $tr.deg._{M_i} M_{i+1} = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(M_{i+1}/M_i)$.
<!-- end cor-21 -->
<!-- head-80: body_md -->
Since $F$ is inversive, and $L_{{\rm res \,}}$ is algebraically closed, by \ref{vt2} and \ref{inv-fin}, $L_{{\rm res \,}}$ is also inversive.  Thus for any $d \geq 1$, ${\rm res \,} ( L^{\sigma^{d}}) = {\rm res \,} (L)$.
By \ref{vt1}, ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(\widehat{L} / \widehat{L}^{\sigma^{d}}) = rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} (\Q-si / \sigma^d(\Q-si)) = d$.   

 To show that (1) implies (2),  we may assume $K=K^a$. 
 By \ref{res-lift}, there exists a field of representatives $  F_r \leq \widehat{K}$ for the residue map of $\widehat{K}$.  We have 
$tr.  deg_F F_r = tr. deg._F K_{{\rm res \,}}$.  Let $K_r = F_rK$.

 By \ref{res-lift} again, applied to $\widehat{L}$ over $K_r$, there exists a difference field $F_r \leq L_1$ such that  ${\rm res \,}: L_1 \to L_{{\rm res \,}}$
is an isomorphism.    Let $K_1 = K_r L_1$.
Then $tr. deg._{K_r} K_1 \leq e_{{\rm res \,}}$; equality holds by 
comparing the residue fields.  Thus (b).  

Now over $K_1$, \ref{lift-val} applies, and gives $K_2$ 
with (c,d).  We have $K \leq \widehat{L}^ {\sigma^{e_2}}$,
and $e_1 \leq rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} {\, \rm val \,}( \widehat{L}^ {\sigma^{e_2}} / K)$;
so
$  e_1 + e_2 \leq  rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} ({\, \rm val \,}(\widehat{L} )/ {\, \rm val \,} K) =
 rk_{\hbox{\msbmten Q}} ({\, \rm val \,} L / {\, \rm val \,} K) $.  Thus (e).

(2) obviously implies (3), with $K'=K_2 \widehat{K}$.  To go from (3) to (4), let 
$K'$ be as in (3).  By \ref{char-comp}, $\widehat{L} \simeq
\widehat{(L_{{\rm res \,}}(t)_\sigma)^a}$, $\widehat{K'} = \widehat{L}^{\sigma^{e_2}} = 
\widehat{(L_{{\rm res \,}}(t^{e_2})_\sigma)^a}$.  
Let $M  = \widehat{(L_{{\rm res \,}}(t^{e_2})_\sigma)^a} (t)$.
Then $\widehat{M} = \widehat{L}$ and $tr. deg._{\widehat{K'}}(M) = e_2$.

(4) implies (1) since ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}$ is additive in towers, bounded by
transcendence degree, and vanishes for completions (${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}_K \widehat{K} = 0$.)
                                                                                                                                           
                                                    
                                       
                                                                             



The final conclusion follows from (4) by taking $e ={rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K)$.
We obtain $M_0,\ldots,M_5$ with 
$M_{i+1} = \widehat{M_i}$ for even $i<5$, and 
$tr.deg._{M_1}M_2 + tr. deg._{M_3} M_4 \leq e$.
But $e = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(M_2/M_1) + {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(M_4/M_3)$, and 
$ {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(M_{i+1}/M_i) \leq
tr.deg._{M_{i+1}}M_i$; so all inequalities must
be equalities.
  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-80 -->
<!-- cor-22: body_md -->
\label{vrk-dec}  Let $L$ be a  transformal valued field of transformal dimension $1$ over an inversive
 difference field $F$, with value group $\Q-si$.   Let $K$ be a nontrivially valued subfield of $L$.    
Let $K'$ be an extension of $K $ within some $\omega$-increasing transformal valued field   containing $L$;
assume $tr. deg._K K' < \infty$.   
Then ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}} (L/K') \leq {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K)$.
<!-- end cor-22 -->
<!-- head-81: body_md -->
Note that taking algebraic closure or completion does
not change ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}$.  We will thus  assume all these fields are algebraically closed; and we will prove a more general statement, 
allowing $L$ to be the completion of a transformal valued field of transformal dimension $1$.

  All residue fields are therefore also algebraically
closed and, being extensions of $K_{{\rm res \,}}$ of transformal
transcendence degree $0$, are inversive.  Note 
(say by \ref{char-comp}) that   $L' = \widehat{K'L}$
is also  the completion of a transformal valued field of transformal dimension $1$.

If $K \leq M \leq  \widehat{L}$, then ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K) = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/M) + {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(M/K)$, and ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K') = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/MK') + {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(M/K')$;
so the lemma for $M/K ; K'$ and for $L/M; MK'$,   implies the statement for $L/K; K'$.  By \ref{vrk}, we may thus
assume one of the following cases holds:  \begin{enumerate}
  \item $L \leq \widehat{K}$
  \item  $tr.deg._K (L) = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}} (L/K)$
                        

\end{enumerate}

In case (1), $LK' \leq \widehat{K'}$, so ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K') = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(\widehat{K'L} / \widehat{K'}) = 0$.  

In case (2), ${rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}}(L/K') \leq tr.deg._{K'}(K'L) \leq tr.deg. _K (L) = {rk_{{\, \rm val \,}}} (L/K)$.

                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                     
                                           
\hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-81 -->
<!-- example-9: body_md -->
In \ref{vrk-dec}, the hypothesis that the value group of $L$ is   $\hbox{\msbmten Q}_\sigma$ is necessary.
<!-- end example-9 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{domin} Let $K=K^a$ be a  transformal valued field of  transformal dimension $1$ over $F$,
with value group $\hbox{\msbmten Q}_\sigma$.  Let 
  $L$ be a   transformal valued field extension  transformal dimension $0$ over $K$.
 Let $\bar{K}$ be an  immediate extension of $K$.  Then $L,\bar{K}$ (and even  $\widehat{L},\bar{K}$) 
 are almost orthogonal over $K$ as valued fields.
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- head-82: body_md -->
The value group ${\Gamma}(K)={\Gamma}(\bar{K})$
is cofinal in ${\Gamma}(L)$, since if $a \in L$ has valuation $> {\Gamma}(K)$ then it must be transformally transcendental 
over $K$.

It follows in particular that  the completion $\widehat{L}$ embeds uniquely into $\widehat{M}$.  From this,
once we show that $L,\bar{K}$ are almost orthogonal over $K$,  almost orthogonality of  $ \widehat{L},\bar{K}$ over $K$ follows.  

                                                                                  
                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                      
                                                                             

By \ref{vrk}, there exists a tower 
$K= K_0 \leq \cdots \leq K_6 = \widehat{L}$  of difference field extensions of $K$, 
with $K_{i+1}$ purely ramified or purely inertial over $K_i$, or contained in $\widehat{K_i}$.  (Namely $K \leq K_r \leq K_1 \leq K_2 \leq \widehat{K_2} \leq M \leq \widehat{L}$; with $M$ as in \ref{vrk} (4).) 
The proposition 
follows from  \ref{domin-val}.

 

  
{\bf Discussion}   

This can be formulated in terms of domination for  types of $ACVF_K$, or quantifier-free types of the language
of valued fields over $K$;  as in the Remark following {Lemma \ref{domin-val}}.  
                                                                                                      
                                                                                             
                                                                                  
  
This implies the existence of 
canonical base change of $L/K$ to  extensions $K'$ of $K$ as transformally valued fields, relative to a base change in ${\rm res \,}(L)$ 
 and
in ${\, \rm val \,}(L)$ making ${\, \rm val \,}(L),{\, \rm val \,}(K')$ independent over ${\, \rm val \,}(K)$; in particular this applies when ${\, \rm val \,}(K') = {\, \rm val \,}(K)$,
more generally when $({\, \rm val \,}(K') \cap \hbox{\msbmten Q}(\sigma) {\, \rm val \,}(K))$ and $({\, \rm val \,}(L) \cap \hbox{\msbmten Q}(\sigma) {\, \rm val \,}(K))$ intersect 
in ${\, \rm val \,}(K)$ within $\hbox{\msbmten Q}(\sigma){\, \rm val \,}(K)$.      But note that in the example above, restricted to 
finitely generated approximations, this condition will not hold.  In any case, this material will not be used in the present paper.


\end{paragraph}
\end{subsection}                 

\begin{subsection}{Finite generation of the value group}

In this subsection, $L$ is an  $\omega$-increasing transformal valued field of 
transformal dimension $1$ over $F$.   We further assume $L $ is a finitely generated difference field extension of $F$.


The results of the present subsection will not be used in the present paper. 

A valued field $K$ is said to be {\em Abhyankar} over a trivially valued subfield $F$ if the transcendence degree of $K$ equals the sum of the transcendence degree $t$ of
the residue field extension, and the dimension $ {\rm dim \, } _{ram}(K/F)$ over $\hbox{\msbmten Q}$ of $\hbox{\msbmten Q} {\otimes} {\Gamma}(K) $.  It is {\em strongly} Abhyankar if 
$tr.deg._F(K) = t + rk_{ram}(K/F)$; equivalently, $K$ is Abhyankar, and in addition the value group ${\Gamma}(K)$ contains a strictly increasing chain of convex subgroups,
with quotients embeddable in $\hbox{\msbmten Q}$>  
   A subfield of a (strongly) Abhyankar valued field is always (strongly) Abhyankar over $F$.  Also if $KF'$ is (strongly) Abhyankar over $F'$,
where $F'/F$ is a trivially valued field extension, then $K/F$ is (strongly) Abhyankar.  A finitely generated Abhyankar extension has finitely generated value group and residue field.  



\begin{lem} \label{abh}   Every finitely generated subfield of $L$ is strongly Abhyankar over $F$.  \end{lem}
<!-- end head-82 -->
<!-- lem-51: body_md -->
\label{abh}   Every finitely generated subfield of $L$ is strongly Abhyankar over $F$.
<!-- end lem-51 -->
<!-- head-83: body_md -->
By {Lemma \ref{vt1}}, the value group of $L$ is contained in $\hbox{\msbmten Q}_\sigma$.  Then condition (1) of  {Lemma \ref{char-comp}} holds for $\widehat{L^a}$; hence by (3) of that lemma,
$L \leq \widehat{F'(t)_\sigma^a}$ for an appropriate trivially valued field $F'$.   By (2) of the same lemma, we may take $t \in L$.   By the remarks above on Abhyankar extensions, it suffices to show (re-denoting $F'$ by $F$):

{\noindent \bf Claim }{}  Let ${K} \leq \widehat{F(t)_\sigma^a}$ be a finitely generated extension field of $F$.  Then ${K}$ is an 
Abhyankar extension of $F$.  

\begin{proof}  Let $t_n = \sigma^n(t)$.
The value group $v({K}^*)$ of ${K}$ is contained in a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Q}$-subspace of $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$.  
Hence it is contained, for some $m$, in the convex hull $C$ of $\hbox{\msbmten Q} v(t_n)$.  There is a natural 
place on $\widehat{F(t)_\sigma^a}$, with residue field $F(t_0,\ldots,t_n)^a$, and value group $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma] / C$.
The residue map $r$ of this place annihilates only elements $x$ with $v(x)>C$; thus it is injective
on ${K}$; moreover it defines a valued field isomorphism on ${K}$ into its image.  As every subfield of
$F(t_0,\ldots,t_n)^a$ is Abhyankar over $F$, the claim and the lemma are proved.  

 \hfill $\Box$ \break \end{proof}
<!-- end head-83 -->
<!-- lem-52: body_md -->
\label{vt1fg}  Let  $L$ be an $\omega$-increasing transformal valued field of 
transformal dimension $1$ over $F$.   Assume    $L $ is a finitely generated difference field extension of $F$.   Then ${\, \rm val \,}(L)$ is isomorphic to a
$\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-submodule of $\Z-si$.
<!-- end lem-52 -->
<!-- head-84: body_md -->
Let  
$L_0$ be a subfield of $L$,
finitely generated over $F$ as a field,   generating $L$ as a difference field.  
                                                   
Let    $L_n$ be the subfield of $L$ generated by $ \cup_{k \leq n   } \sigma^k(L_0)$.
Then $[L_{n+1}: L_n] \leq [L_1:L_0] < \infty$.   Let $A_n = {\, \rm val \,} L_n$.
Then $A_0 \subset A_1 \subset \ldots \subset {\, \rm val \,} L^a \simeq \hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$, 
$A_0$ is finitely generated (using {Lemma \ref{abh}}), and $ A_{n+1} / A_n$ is bounded.  By  {Lemma \ref{vt1}} and  lemma
\ref{vt1-0}  below, ${\, \rm val \,} L$ is a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module.   And
by \ref{vt1-2}, every finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$ submodule of $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[\sigma]$ is contained in a free $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module of rank one. 
\hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-84 -->
<!-- lem-53: body_md -->
\label{vt1-0}  Let $B_0 \subseteq B_1 \subseteq \ldots $ 
  be   finitely generated subgroups of
  $\hbox{\msbmten Q}[T]$ such that   $TB_n \subseteq B_{n+1}$, with $B_{n+1} / B_n  $ finite
and bounded.  Then $B = \cup_n  B_n$ is a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$-module.
<!-- end lem-53 -->
<!-- head-85: body_md -->
Let $A_i= (B_i + \hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]) / \hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$, $A= \cup_i A_i$.  We will show $A_i$ is finitely generated as
a  $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$-module.  It follows that $B+ \hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$ is a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$-module; and by Noetherianity of $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$,
so is $B$.    Note that $A_{n+1} / A_n$ is finite and bounded, and $TA_n \subseteq A_{n+1}$.  

We use induction on $m = \limsup _n  \left|  A_{n+1} /  A_n   \right| $.   If $A \neq 0$,
there exists  $c \in A$, $ c \neq 0$, $lc = 0$, $l$ prime.  Say $c \in A_{n_0}$.

{\noindent \bf Claim } Let $E=E_l = \{x: l x=0 \}$.  Then for $n \geq n_0$, $E \cap A_{n+1} \not \subseteq A_n$.

Suppose the claim is false; then any $x \in E \cap A_n$ satisfies $Tx \in E \cap A_{n+1} = E \cap A_n$.  Thus $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T] c \subset A_n$.  But $A_n$ is a finitely
generated group, while $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T] c $ is not:  $c,Tc,\ldots$ are
$\hbox{\msbmten Z}/l \hbox{\msbmten Z}$ - linearly independent.  A contradiction.

Thus the natural surjective map $e_l: A_{n+1}/A_n \to lA_{n+1} / lA_n$, $e_l(x)=lx$,
 is not 
injective, for $n \geq n_0$.  So $\limsup _n  \left|  lA_{n+1} /  lA_n   \right|  < m$. 
By induction,  $lA$ is a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$-module. 

Now $E_l  / ( \hbox{\msbmten Z}[T] c)$ is finite; indeed $E_l \simeq ( \hbox{\msbmten Z}/l \hbox{\msbmten Z})[T]$, so $ E_l  / ( \hbox{\msbmten Z}[T] c) \simeq ( \hbox{\msbmten Z}/l \hbox{\msbmten Z})[T] / f$
for some nonzero polynomial $f(T)$.  Thus $(A \cap E_l) / (\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]c)$ is 
finite.  Since $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]c$ is a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[T]$-module, so is
$A \cap E_l = \ker (x \mapsto lx)$.  We saw $lA$ was finitely generated; hence
so is $A$.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-85 -->
<!-- lem-54: body_md -->
\label{vt1-2}  Let $M$ be a finitely generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-submodule of $\Q-si$.  Let 
${\widetilde{M}}$ be the union of all submodules $N$ of $\Q-si$ with $N/M$ finite.  Then ${\widetilde{M}}$ is
1-generated.
<!-- end lem-54 -->
<!-- head-86: body_md -->
If $M$ is generated by $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, $m_ia_i \in \hbox{\msbmten Z}_\sigma$ for some
$0< m_i \in \hbox{\msbmten N}$; so each $a_i \in \hbox{\msbmten Z}_\sigma[1/m]$, where $m = \Pi_i m_i$.
  Thus   $M \subset N$ for some principal $N   \leq \Q-si$.



{\noindent \bf Claim }  For any  ideal $J$ of $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$, there exists a principal ideal $J'$  containing $J$ with $J'/J$ finite.
<!-- end head-86 -->
<!-- head-87: body_md -->
$J$ is $k$-generated for some finite $k$.  The claim reduces inductively to the case $k=2$.
So say $J= \hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma](a,b)$.  Since $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$ is a  unique factorization domain,  we
 may write $a=a'c,b=b'c$ with no prime element of $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$
dividing both $a'$ and $b'$.  As $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$ has
Krull dimension $2$, $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]/(a',b')$ must be finite.  

Let $J' = \hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]c$.  Then $a',b' $ annihilate $J'/J$, so that  $J'/J$ is a quotient
of $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]/(a',b')$, and hence is also  finite.

Actually, $J'$ is unique:

{\noindent \bf Claim } If $N \leq \Q-si$ is principal, then $\Q-si $ has no  $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-submodules $N'$ such that 
$N \subseteq N'$, and $N'/N$ is finite and nonzero.

 For otherwise it would have a finitely
generated one, so again one contained in a principal $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module.  Thus it suffices
to show that if $J$ is a submodule of $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$ containing a principal module $K$, then $J/K$ 
is zero or infinite.  If $J/K$ is nonzero and finite, so is $J'/K$, where $J'/J$ is finite and $J'$ is principal.
So $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]/f\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$ is finite nonzero; but this is clearly absurd.  

Thus ${\widetilde{M}} \subset N$.  Let $I = \{r \in \hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]: rN \subset {\widetilde{M}}\}$.  So ${\widetilde{M}} = IN$. By 
definition of ${\widetilde{M}}$, if $I'/I$ is finite then $I'=I$.  Thus by the Claim $I$ is principal.  So   ${\widetilde{M}}$ is 1-generated.

                                                                                                                         
                                                                                           
                                                                                                
                                                                                                    
                                                                                                
                                                                                                    
                                                                                                               
                                                                                                       
                                                            
                                                   
\hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-87 -->
<!-- example-10: body_md -->
${\, \rm val \,}(L)$ need not itself be free.
<!-- end example-10 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
Let
  $F$ be a difference field of characteristic  $0$, closed under roots.     Let   $L$ be a   
  transformal discrete valuation ring   over $F$, Henselian as a valued field.
   Then $L$   has a finite $\sigma$-invariant extension $M$, whose value group is
isomorphic to $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- head-88: body_md -->
By \ref{vt1-2}, ${\, \rm val \,} L \subset {\widetilde{M}}$ for some free 1-generated $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module ${\widetilde{M}}$ with ${\widetilde{M}} / {\, \rm val \,} L$
finite;
we have ${\, \rm val \,} L = I {\widetilde{M}}$ for some ideal $I$, and necessarily $n \in I$ for some $n >0$. 

 Since $L$ is Henselian and $F$ is closed under roots, the homorphism
 $val: L^* {\to >} {\, \rm val \,} L$  is a surjection.  It induces a surjection 
$$(L^*)^n {\to >} n {\, \rm val \,} L$$
Let $H$ be the pullback of $n {\widetilde{M}} \subset {\, \rm val \,} L$.  We have $\sigma(H) \subset H$; and 
  $$H/(L^*)^n \simeq n {\widetilde{M}} / n {\, \rm val \,} L \simeq {\widetilde{M}} / {\, \rm val \,}(L)$$
In particular,  $H/(L^*)^n$ is finite.    By Kummer theory, there exists a unique Galois extension
$K$ of $L$, such that $(K^*)^n \cap L = H$, and   $[K:L] = [H:  (L^*)^n] = {\widetilde{M}} / {\, \rm val \,} L$.   Now $\sigma(K)L$
is also a Galois extension of $L$, generated by $n$'th roots of elements of $H$; hence it is contained
in $K$; so $K$ is a difference field.   
 Tracing back the isomorphisms we see that ${\widetilde{M}} \subset {\, \rm val \,}(K) $, so ${\widetilde{M}} = {\, \rm val \,}(K)$. \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-88 -->
<!-- rem-7: body_md -->
\label{vt1c2z}  Let $M \subset \hbox{\msbmten Z}-si$ be a $\hbox{\msbmten Z}[\sigma]$-module.      Let $Y$ be a downward-closed subset of $M$.  
  Then for some nonzero convex subgroup
$S$ of $M$, and $0 \leq a \in \hbox{\msbmten R}[\sigma]$, 
$$Y  = \{y \in M:  (\exists c \in S) y \leq a+c \}$$
<!-- end rem-7 -->
<!-- lem-55: body_md -->
\label{res-dom}  Let $D \subset D'=D[a]$ be difference domains;
$a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ a tuple of generators of $D'$ as a difference $D$-algebra.  
 Assume $\sigma(a) \in D[a]^{int}$ ( the integral closure of the domain $D[a]$.).  Then for large enough $m$, for 
any morphism $h: D' \to K$,
with $(K,R,v)$ an $m$-increasing transformal valuation field, if $h(D) \subset R$ then $h(D') \in R$.
<!-- end lem-55 -->
<!-- head-89: body_md -->
For each $i$, $\sigma(a_i)$ is a root of a monic  polynomial 
$f_i = \sum_{l=0}^{d_i} c_{i,l}X^l \in D[a][X]$.
The coefficients $c_{i,l}$ are themselves polynomials in $a$ 
over $D$; take $m$ bigger than the total degree of all these polynomials.
Then if $v$ is a valuation, with $v(d) \geq 0$ for $d \in D$ and $v(a_i) \geq  \delta$ for each $i$, (where $\delta < 0$), then  for each $i,l$,
$v(c_{i,l}) > m \delta$.  

  Assume  $(K,R,{\, \rm val \,})$ is $m$-increasing, and $h(D) \subset R$.
We may replace $D,D'$ by their images under $h$, and assume 
$h$ is the inclusion.
Say ${\, \rm val \,}(ha_1) \leq {\, \rm val \,}(ha_2) \leq \ldots \leq val(ha_n)$.  We have to show that $\delta={\, \rm val \,}(a_1) \geq 0$.    
Otherwise,  as the (monic) leading monomial of $f_i(\sigma(a_i))$ cannot have
valuation less than all other monomials, we have $d_1 val(\sigma(a_1)) \geq   {\, \rm val \,}(c_{1,l})+l val(\sigma(a_1)) $ for some
$l< d_1$.  Thus $(d_1-l) val(\sigma(a_1)) \geq {\, \rm val \,}(c_{1,l}) > m \delta$.
So  ${\, \rm val \,} \sigma({a_1}^{-1}) \leq m {\, \rm val \,} {a_1}^{-1}$.  This contradicts the assumption
that ${\, \rm val \,}$ is $m$-increasing, and proves the lemma.  \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-89 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\  \label{res-inj-not}
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- lem-56: body_md -->
\label{res-inj}  Let $(K,R,\bar{K})$ be a  strictly increasing transformal valued field. 
Let $X$ be a finitely generated quasi-projective difference  scheme over $R$, $X_0 = X {\otimes}_R {\bar{K}}$.    Assume the  reduction sequence map $X_0 \to  B_1X_0$ is
unramified (\ref{res-inj-not}).  Then the residue map $X(R) \to X({\bar{K}})$ is injective.
<!-- end lem-56 -->
<!-- head-90: body_md -->
Consider first the special case   $X = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } R[x]/f(x)$, $f(x) = x  + g(x) + h(x)  \in R[x]_\sigma$; 
where  $g $ has coefficients in the maximal ideal $M$ of $R$, and $h$ is a sum of monomials $x^{\nu}$, $\nu \in \hbox{\msbmten N}[\sigma]$, $\nu > 1$.  Let  $a,b \in X(R)$ with ${\rm res \,}(a)={\rm res \,}(b)$; we will
  show $a=b$.  We may assume $b=0$.  Then 
   ${\rm res \,}(a)=0$ so ${\, \rm val \,}(a) > 0$; but then 
   ${\, \rm val \,} (h(a)) > {\, \rm val \,} (a)$, and also ${\, \rm val \,} (g(a)) > {\, \rm val \,} (a)$, so $f(a)  = 0$ implies
$a=0$.   

In general, we may assume $X = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } A$;  $X_0 = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } A_0$, 
$B_1X_0 = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } {A_0}'$, with   $A_0= A {\otimes}_R {\bar{K}} $, ${A_0}' = \sigma(A_0)$,
with   $ X_0 \to  B_1X_0$  a   standard  
unramified map (\ref{res-inj-not}):
  $A_0$ has generators $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ over $ {A_0}'$, admitting relations  $F_1,\ldots,F_n$, 
   where $(F_{i}) \in {A_0}'[y_1,\ldots,y_n] $ has 
invertible Jacobian matrix $\det (\partial_{y_i}F_j) \in G_m({A_0}')$.

Complete $y_1,\ldots, y_n$ to a system   of  generators of $A_0$ over $\bar{K}$; since
the $y_i$ already generate $A$ over $ {A_0}'$, the additional generators $y_j$ may
be chosen from $ {A_0}'$.  Each new $y_j$ solves the inhomogeneous linear polynomial
$Y_j-y_j \in {A_0}'[Y_j]$; adding these generators and relations to the system clearly leaves
the Jacobian invertible.

Now the coefficients of the $F_i$ lie in $\sigma(A_0)$, so they may themselves be expressed
as difference polynomials in the $y_i$, indeed in the $\sigma(y_i)$.  Replacing the coefficients
by these polynomials, we may assume that $F_i \in {\bar K}[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ has coefficients
in $\bar{K}$, rather than in $\sigma(A_0)$.  If we convene that $\partial \sigma(Y_j) / \partial Y_k = 0$,
the Jacobian matrix remains invertible.  


  Lift  the generators $y_i$ to $x_i \in A$.  Then any element of $A$ can be written as a difference 
polynomial over $\sigma(A)$ in the $x_i$, up to an element of ${\cal M} A = \ker A \to A {\otimes}_R {\bar{K}} $.
(Here ${\cal M}$ is the maximal ideal of $R$.  )
So $A$ has generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n,x_{n+1},\ldots,x_N$, where for $i>n$ the image of $x_i $ 
in $A_0$ is $y_i=0$.  We still have $A_0= {A_0}'[y_1,\ldots,y_N]/ (F_1,\ldots,F_N)$, where
$F_i = y_i$ for $i>n$.   Lift the $F_i$ to $f_i \in \sigma(A)[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$.  Then
in $A$ we have a relation $f_i(x_1,\ldots,x_N) = g_i(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$, where $g_i$ 
 has coefficients in ${\cal M}$.  

Consider two elements $e=(e_1,\ldots,e_N), e'=(e'_1,\ldots,e'_N)$ of $X(R)$ specializing to the same point
of $X_0$.  Replacing $x_i$ by $x_i-e'_i$,  we may assume 
$e'=0$.      Suppose $e \neq 0$; let $\min_{i} {\, \rm val \,} (e_i) =  \beta > 0$.   In these coordinates,
let $L_i$ be the linear (monomials of order $1$) part of $f_i$.  The $L_i$ are then the rows
of an invertible matrix $L$ over $R$, and $L_i x - g_i(x) + h_i(x) = 0$, where 
$h_i$   is a sum of $\sigma$-monomials of degree $>1$.  Since $e \in X(R)$, we 
have $Le - g(e) + h(e) = 0$.   (Where $g,h$ are the matrices of $\sigma$-polynomials whose
rows are $g_i,h_i$.)

Now $\min_i {\, \rm val \,} (\sigma(e_i)) = \sigma(\beta) > \beta $, so ${\, \rm val \,} h_i(e)   > \beta$.
Also ${\, \rm val \,} g_i(e) > \beta$.  Writing $e = - G^{-1} ( g(e) + h(e))$, we see that $\min_i {\, \rm val \,} (e_i) > \beta$,
a contradiction.     \hfill $\Box$ \break
<!-- end head-90 -->
<!-- lem-57: body_md -->
\label{res-surj}      Let $(K,R,\bar{K})$ be a  strictly increasing transformal valued field,
 with $K$ maximally complete as a valued field.  
Let $X = {\rm Spec^\sigma \, } R[X]/ (F, J {^{-1}})$, where $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$, where the $f_i$
are difference polynomials over $R$, and $J= \det \partial f_i / \partial x_j $.   
Then $X(R) \to X({\bar{K}})$ is surjective.
<!-- end lem-57 -->
